records.current_summary: The dossier's only regional signal for this department is administrative-capacity rather than incident evidence: Regional Management Resolution R.G.R. No 000757-2024-GR-LAMB shows the regional government regulating education-administration competences via its regional education directorate - the lever through which national 'gender ideology' disputes reach schools. No trans-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement pattern was found for this department; it is otherwise assessed at the national position (±0.02).

sources.claim: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): Congress's Women and Family Commission unanimously approved a bill barring trans people from public restrooms of the sex other than their birth sex (bills 6506 and 8457, by two governing-bloc legislators), with exceptions for custody situations, medical care, and accompanying elderly, under-12 or disabled people; the initiative also requires removing restroom signage ambiguous about who may enter. Trigger was a July 2023 complaint about gendered toilet labels at Lima's international airport. National law - applies in Puno as everywhere; still requires full plenary approval.

IDEHPUCP human-rights institute analysis (15 April 2025), 'Legalised discrimination': on 2 April 2025 Congress's plenary approved, waiving a second vote, the children's-sexual-rights law, fused by the Women and Family Commission with the trans bathroom-restriction bills; critiques the measure as institutionalised discrimination against trans people under national human-rights standards.

Agencia Presentes (22 July 2024): the UPCH TLGBI Rights Observatory's annual report records 54 LGBTI killings and 170 rights violations 2020-2023, trans women the most affected (30 of 54), gay men 23, one lesbian; 19 homicides in 2023 alone (12 trans women, 7 gay men). Documents the Feb 2023 abduction of trans sex worker Rubí Torres Silvano, 31, from central Lima by the Los Gallegos gang and her murder in Carabayllo with ~30 gunshot wounds, within a pattern of gang extortion of sex workers. National stats - no department-specific cut.

records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): the Congress's Women and Family Commission approved unanimously the dictamen of bills 6506/2023-CR (Montoya) and 8457/2023-CR (Muñante), which prohibit entry to public sanitary services designated to the opposite sex at birth (exceptions: custody, medical attention, accompanying a person under 12, an elderly person or a person with a disability) and prohibit ambiguous bathroom signage; the dictamen still required plenary support. Context: in July 2023 a complaint about the gendered signage at Jorge Chávez International Airport led to the labels being changed to 'mujeres/hombres en su diversidad'. Activist Gianna Camacho states no official statistics of trans violence in women's bathrooms exist, and enforcement would rest on individual security staff judging IDs.

IDEHPUCP bulletin, analysis by Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte (15 Apr 2025): on Wednesday 2 April 2025 the Plenary of Congress approved, exempting it from a second vote, the dictamen of the law strengthening the right to the sexual indemnity of children and adolescents (merger of bills 6505/2023-CR and 8457/2023-CR). Article 5.1 of the bill bans entry and use of public sanitary services to any person whose biological sex does not match the service's designated sex, with narrow exceptions for accompaniment/assistance and legal or judicial mandates. The bulletin reads the provision as a direct violation of equality and non-discrimination (Political Constitution art. 2.2, American Convention art. 1.1) in line with IACtHR OC-24/17, and as validating stereotypes about trans people.

Agencia Presentes (22 Jul 2024) on the Annual Report of the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI of the Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia: 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023; more than half the homicide victims were trans women (30), then gay men (23) and one lesbian woman; yearly homicides 2020: 12 (8 trans women), 2021: 10, 2022: 13, 2023: 19 (12 trans women). Killings involved extreme cruelty (multiple gunshots, stabblings, throat-cuttings); rights violations peaked at 61 in 2020 (43 in 2022, 34 in 2023, 32 in 2021), trans women again the most affected. Includes testimony that in Feb 2023 extortion gang 'Los Gallegos' abducted sex worker Rubí Torres Silvano (31) in central Lima and killed her in Carabayllo with ~30 shots, a case of the pimping-mafia violence the movement identifies as the main trans-femicide driver.

records.name: Ucayali
records.current_summary: No region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division - the research dossier lists it among the units with no sub-national signal, so the national evidence applies: the congressional Women and Family Committee approved bills banning trans people from public restrooms in early 2025 (floor vote pending), and the national university observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023, more than half of the homicide victims trans women (30 of 54). The absence of local findings reflects Peru's lack of hate-crime statistics rather than any positive local difference.

sources.claim: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): the congressional Women and Family Committee unanimously approved bills (from Montoya and Muñante) banning trans people from public restrooms, with exceptions for custody, medical need, and accompanying children under 12 or elderly/disabled persons, plus a ban on ambiguous bathroom signage; a floor vote is pending. Recounts the July 2023 complaint over 'feminine/masculine identity' bathroom labels at Jorge Chávez airport and LGTBIQ activist Gianna Camacho's objection that the measures weaponise stigma against trans people.

IDEHPUCP human-rights bulletin (15 April 2025): legal analysis of Congress's proposed prohibition of trans people from public restrooms, based on bills 6505/2023-CR and 8457/2023-CR fused at the Women and Family Committee; contextualises it alongside the 2 April 2025 Plenary approval (exempted from a second vote) of the children's sexual-indemnity law, framing the package as legalised discrimination against trans access to public space.

records.name: Moquegua
records.current_summary: No documented sub-national signal for Moquegua: the country dossier lists this department among the regions where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. What binds Moquegua is the national frame: a congressional bill package (6506/8457, committee-approved February 2025) would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities of the opposite sex at birth, and national data record 54 killings and 170 rights-violation cases of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023 with trans women most affected and hate crimes rising - no regional deviation documented either way.

sources.claim: Infobae national news report (20 Feb 2025): the congressional committee on women and family approved unanimously the report backing bills 6506 and 8457 (lawmakers Montoya and Munante), which bar trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite their birth sex - with exceptions for custody, medical care and accompanying children under 12, elderly or disabled people - and require unambiguous facility signage; the opinion still needs full-chamber approval. An LGBTI activist quoted calls the measure discriminatory.

IDEHPUCP (human-rights institute, Pontifical Catholic University of Peru) bulletin: academic critique of the congressional bathroom ban - argues the law implicitly brands trans people as a sexual risk to minors in facilities, citing a lawmaker's ridicule of trans bathroom use; part of the institute's coverage of legalised discrimination (incl. INDECOPI discrimination rulings).

Presentes news report (22 Jul 2024) on the UPCH Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI annual report: 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023, with trans women the most affected group and hate crimes rising; includes testimony on the February 2023 murder of a trans woman kidnapped from downtown Lima and shot dead by a criminal gang in Carabayllo.
